content:
AirPods are among Apple's most interesting products. The demand for these earbuds was largely created by the company removing the headphone jack a decade ago, and now most people carry these almost magical earbuds, doing far more than just playing audio. AirPods offer industry-leading noise cancellation while also doubling as hearing aids, and they get better almost every year.

Despite all these great things about AirPods, there's one thing that bothers me about them, especially since it could easily be fixed with a software update.

Currently, if your AirPods need charging and your iPhone is plugged in to charge, the system will pop up a prompt suggesting you charge your AirPods at the same time. Apple does this because it thinks charging your AirPods while your iPhone is charging won't be too much trouble, and this prompt has saved me countless times, preventing me from unknowingly using AirPods that are out of battery.

AirPods frequently die in the charging case

If you've used AirPods for a while, you're probably quite familiar with this problem: something gets stuck between the charging contacts in the case and one of the AirPods, so when you take them out you find that one side is completely dead. This often ruins the mood for a walk, a trip to work, or anything else you're doing.

At least for me, adding a notification to alert users when one AirPod isn't charging is an obvious move. If one AirPod is in the case and the other one isn't detected as being worn, there's a good chance it's in the case but not charging, and Apple could remind users to adjust the AirPod's position or check if something is blocking it in the case.

This big annoyance that could have been easily solved would then be another example of Apple's magical touch, giving you an early heads-up that one of your AirPods isn't charging so you don't find out too late.

Hopefully Apple can add this feature in a future iOS update. The latest generation AirPods Pro 3 is currently on sale at $179, worth considering if you don't already own a pair.
